defs.def: a mixture of finely chopped meat, fat, bread, etc. in a long tube of skin, cooked and eaten whole or served cold in thin slices 香肠；腊肠

ex.s: However, though it’s nice to get a few cents off a pack of sausages, it would help even more if they could sometimes   61   (offer) in smaller packs.
ex.t: 然而，尽管一包香肠能便宜几分钱不错，但如果它们有时能以更小包装（第61空，offer）出售，会更有帮助。

ex.s: Even the biggest sausage fan doesn’t want to eat them every day.
ex.t: 即便是最大的香肠爱好者，也不想每天都吃香肠。

ex.s: They pulled the sausage beyond the dog’s reach.
ex.t: 他们把香肠拉到狗够不到的地方。

ex.s: I still don’t think that anything can beat my mum’s homemade sausages, though.
ex.t: 不过，我仍然认为没有什么能打败我妈妈的自制香肠。

ex.s: Dad can cook a super "full English breakfast "of bacon, eggs, beans, sausages and toast with butter if Mum and I can find a way to get him into the kitchen!
ex.t: 如果我和妈妈能想办法把爸爸弄进厨房，他就能做一顿超级棒的“全套英式早餐”——熏肉、鸡蛋、豆子、香肠和黄油吐司！

ex.s: Traditional accompaniments such as Yorkshire pudding, sausages, stuffing and gravy are also served.
ex.t: 还提供传统的配菜，如约克郡布丁、香肠、填料和肉汁。

ex.s: A simple restaurant was where he usually had the same meal of sausages, eggs and coffee.
ex.t: 一家简单的餐厅是他通常吃同样一顿香肠、鸡蛋和咖啡的地方。

ex.s: Build up your vocabulary A a piece of sausage for her dinner.
ex.t: 积累你的词汇量为她的晚餐准备一根香肠。
